about.title: About the app

howto.read_body: Four tabs sit at the foot of the screen: Today for your day's wird, Mushaf for reading, My hifz for what you have memorized and the tools to keep it, and Settings. From Mushaf, choose a surah or a juz to read on its own in the mushaf's pages; at its end you can move to the one after or before. In Settings you can set the view to “Mushaf”, and the app then opens straight onto the last page you read.
howto.listen_body: Tap the page to bring up the session bar, then Start. The ayahs are recited as many times as you choose; the ayah being recited is marked and the page follows it. The bar's “Repeat this ayah three more times” button goes over the current ayah again, and the sleep timer in the session settings pauses the recitation after the minutes you choose, or at the end of a step. Tap the page again to put the bar away.
howto.range_body: Long-press an ayah to hear from it to the end of the surah once, to memorize it alone, or to make it the start or the end of the range. In the session settings you set the range by surah and ayah, and it may end in a later surah.
howto.modes_body: Cumulative: an ayah is repeated, then everything from the start of the range up to it — one ayah, then two, then three. Continuous: the whole range is recited through, then again. No joining: each ayah is repeated on its own.
howto.recall_body: The session settings have Recall rounds: after an ayah is repeated, the app stays silent for its length while you recite it from memory, then plays it once to confirm. And Test the links: at the end of the session each ayah is played, the app falls silent while you recite the one after it from memory, then plays it as the answer.
howto.presets_body: The session settings offer ready ways of working: New portion, Recent review, Old review, Deep drill, and Listen, which recites the range straight through with no testing. Set things as you like, tap “Save as preset” and give it a name, and it becomes a chip beside them; the × on it removes it. On the Today tab you set a range for each of New portion, Recent review and Old review: each stays until you change it, and opens in one tap on its range, worked its own way.
howto.change_body: Speed and pauses change at once. For the reciter, the range, the repeats and the way of joining you are asked: start again, or carry on from the current ayah?
howto.view_body: From Settings or the session settings you can cover the page's words to test yourself as you read: First words keeps the first word of each ayah as a cue, Hidden covers every ayah. Touch a covered word to uncover its ayah.
howto.stumble_body: Long-press an ayah you stumble at and choose “I stumble here”: it is repeated more in your sessions, light dots sit under it, and its surah in Mushaf shows how many such places it has. They are all listed in My hifz under Weak spots.
howto.tasmee_body: In the session settings choose “Recite to a listener” and hand the phone to whoever is listening: they touch the ayah where you slip, and it is noted under Weak spots. Undo takes back the last touch; End finishes.
howto.review_body: When you finish a memorization session, the app asks how well you held it: Solid, Shaky or Forgot. The passage joins your review schedule and comes back when it is due — new passages soon, older ones further apart. What is due appears on Today, and the whole schedule is in My hifz. Turn on Bedtime and morning in Settings, and Today also suggests the day's new portion before you sleep, to hear once more, and the next morning, to recite back.
howto.plan_body: In My hifz, open Memorization plan, then choose what to memorize and in how many days; it is cut into daily portions of about equal length, never splitting an ayah. Today's portion appears on Today, and the plan moves on when you finish it and grade it Solid or Shaky.
howto.similar_body: In an ayah's menu, Similar ayahs names the ayahs that share its wording, and opens them with the shared words shaded. In My hifz, Mutashabihat lists every phrase repeated across ayahs and where each occurs, surah by surah. From a phrase, open the Mutashabihat drill: each ayah is shown as far as the phrase reaches; choose which ayah it is, continue it from memory, then show the rest.
howto.offline_body: Reading never needs a connection. Recitation streams, and you can download a surah from the session settings to listen offline; what you have downloaded is listed in Settings under Saved recitations.
howto.backup_body: Everything is kept on this device alone, with no account. In My hifz, Your practice shows the days you practised, the minutes you listened and what you memorized. Back up progress saves a copy you can send or keep wherever you like, then import on another device, where it is merged with what is there and nothing is removed.
howto.resume_body: The app remembers the last page you read and shows it on Today and in Mushaf, and the reading history keeps the last twenty places. To mark your place yourself, long-press an ayah and choose “I stopped here”; it then becomes Continue reading. If a session stops before it is finished, the session bar offers to carry on from where you had reached. The ring beside each surah shows how much of it you have memorized, and opens the detail ayah by ayah.

onboarding.read_body: Read the whole Quran in the mushaf's own pages, surah by surah or juz by juz, with no connection.
onboarding.method_body: Hear an ayah and repeat it, then the next, then both joined together — one rung at a time, until it holds.
onboarding.control_body: Tap the page to start, and long-press an ayah to choose what to memorize. The ayah being recited is marked, and the page follows it.
onboarding.test_body: The app falls silent while you recite an ayah from memory, then plays it back. It can cover the page so you recite to yourself, or a listener can tap where you slip.
onboarding.review_body: Grade how it went after each session, and the passage comes back when it is due. Set a plan in days, and today's portion and review wait on the home page.
onboarding.similar_body: See ayahs that share their wording side by side and drill telling them apart; the places you stumble are repeated more in your sessions.
onboarding.yours_body: Choose the reciter, the repeats and the way of joining, and pick up whenever you like from where you stopped. No ads, no accounts.
